---
title: "Same Every Time"
---

::: {.ao-story}
A talkative creature sits in the middle of the line. Sometimes it says one thing and sometimes another, and the factory's customers need the same answer every time, as the Automata give. The boasters called this its charm. Decide whether it belongs on the line at all.
:::

::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** you will decide whether an LLM belongs inside a pipeline, and keep the pipeline reproducible if it does.
- **Before you start:** [Script, Model, or LLM](../basecamp/three-kinds-of-machine.html).
- **Time:** about 15 minutes.
:::

You need this before you put a model inside a pipeline. A pipeline earns trust by giving the same answer from the same input. An LLM call can return different text from run to run, so an LLM inside a step changes the pipeline's behaviour.

Keep the LLM out of the run when you can. Use it to write a script, then test the script and run the script. Ask the LLM for the script, read it, run it on a small input where you know the answer, and fix it until the output matches. The script behaves the same every time and you can review it.

If an LLM call really must be a step, contain it. Take an example: assigning a sample-type label to free-text metadata such as "liver carcinoma biopsy". The function wraps the call, and `call_model` is a stub for the model call.

```python
import hashlib, json, logging, pathlib

MODEL, PROMPT_VERSION = "model-x-2026-01", "v3"   # example values
LABELS = {"tumour", "normal", "cell line", "unknown"}
CACHE = pathlib.Path("cache")

def label_sample(text):
    key = hashlib.sha256(f"{MODEL}|{PROMPT_VERSION}|{text}".encode()).hexdigest()
    path = CACHE / f"{key}.json"
    if path.exists():                                  # 1. cache
        return json.loads(path.read_text())["label"]
    label = call_model(text).strip().lower()
    if label not in LABELS:                            # 2. validate
        raise ValueError(f"bad label {label!r} for {text!r}")
    logging.warning("model=%s prompt=%s input=%s label=%s", MODEL, PROMPT_VERSION, key[:12], label)  # 3. log
    CACHE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps({"label": label}))
    return label
```

- **Cache:** the file name is a hash of the model name, the prompt version and the input, so a re-run reads the saved label, and a new model or prompt version asks again.
- **Validate:** the reply must be one of a fixed set of labels, and anything else stops the run.
- **Log:** each fresh call records the model name, the prompt version and a short fingerprint of the input. Pin the model (one fixed version, never "latest"), though a pinned model may still return different text.
- **Keep a human-check sample:** look at a random handful on every run.
- **Keep restricted data away from external models.** Data you may not share must not reach an outside API (a service your code calls over the network).

## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [Reduce hallucinations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it suggests comparing repeated runs, a cheap way to see whether an LLM step gives the same answer each time, and admits such habits reduce but do not remove errors.
- [Containers](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/container): Seqera (Nextflow docs), docs. Why read: it says containerizing a pipeline makes it self-contained and reproducible, and shows setting the container per process.
- [Distribution and Reproducibility](https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/snakefiles/deployment.html): Snakemake, docs. Why read: it covers per-rule conda environments, containers and pinning, the answer to unpinned tools.
- [Conda environments](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/conda): Seqera (Nextflow docs), docs. Why read: it shows pinning tool versions by name in the spec and using lock files for more reproducible environments.
:::
